searchText: It is expected that a client fully supporting optimistic sync tests ignores the `valid` flag Those that are not supporting the format may ignore `on_payload_info` and both will end up with the same fork choice state But should we care about those that are not supporting extended format? If not, then we may just omit `valid: false` when the payload is eventually invalid But are you going to change as well the forkchoice tests? the thing is that if I want to keep the previous forkchoice test-vectors and these sync vectors in the same code, I would much rather have the meaning of `valid: false` being equivalent to `INVALID` Currently the meaning is `valid: true` being equivalent to VALID We want this extension to be backward compatible with the format, so, no changes to forkchoice tests should be made. What would be the `valid` bit for SYNCING then? So currently for our forkchoice tests we use `valid: false` to be equivalent to the payload being `INVALID`. The sync tests break this `valid` flag holds validity status of entire block including payload. The complexity here comes from SYNCING -> INVALID/VALID which makes us think about the third value for a flag OR say that `valid` is strictly about beacon block and payload validity should be derived from its status so `valid: true, status: SYNCING` may turn into `valid: true, status: INVALID` which means that the block is invalid The semanthics we use is: `valid: true` --> We expect no errror from `on_block`... `valid: false` we expect errors from `on_block`. We do not error on SYNCING blocks. Optimistic sync is about "validity" not being binary There's no intrinsic tension here, just that modeling this as true/false creates a false dichotomy We have the full optimistic status from the `status` field. Let me put it in a different way: If I run testvectors from forkchoice the same vectors, but with some blocks being SYNCING and with this format, I should pass the tests without changing my code. This will not happen because of the `valid` field. If all testvectors from forkchoice are also changed to conform to this format then I don't mind at all cause I can just ignore the `valid` check and that's it Ok, I get it, thanks Do we need additional `is_payload_eventually_valid` status? I don't think so: the payload status has all the information we need

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
It is expected that a client fully supporting optimistic sync tests ignores the `valid` flag
Those that are not supporting the format may ignore `on_payload_info` and both will end up with the same fork choice state

But should we care about those that are not supporting extended format? If not, then we may just omit `valid: false` when the payload is eventually invalid

excerpts.content: But are you going to change as well the forkchoice tests? the thing is that if I want to keep the previous forkchoice test-vectors and these sync vectors in the same code, I would much rather have the meaning of `valid: false` being equivalent to `INVALID`

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Currently the meaning is `valid: true` being equivalent to VALID

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: We want this extension to be backward compatible with the format, so, no changes to forkchoice tests should be made. What would be the `valid` bit for SYNCING then?

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
`valid` flag holds validity status of entire block including payload. The complexity here comes from SYNCING -> INVALID/VALID which makes us think about the third value for a flag OR
say that `valid` is strictly about beacon block and payload validity should be derived from its status

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: so `valid: true, status: SYNCING` may turn into `valid: true, status: INVALID` which means that the block is invalid

excerpts.content: The semanthics we use is: `valid: true` --> We expect no errror from `on_block`... `valid: false` we expect errors from `on_block`. We do not error on SYNCING blocks.
